                <h3>Constraining the Progenitor Orbits of Sequential Black-Hole Mergers in Hierarchical Triples: Peters-Based Estimates</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Felix M. Heinze, Zhoujian Cao</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Two black-hole merger events may originate from sequential mergers in a pre-existing hierarchical black-hole triple if their spatial localizations overlap and the remnant mass of the first merger is compatible with a component mass of the second. In this scenario, the inner binary merges first, leaving a remnant that remains bound to the tertiary and subsequently undergoes a second merger. We present a method to constrain the progenitor triple's outer orbit by modeling the gravitational-wave-driven evolution of the remnant-tertiary binary using Peters' equations. Given an assumed upper bound on the recoil velocity of the first merger, the method requires only the black-hole masses, the time delay between the mergers, and the eccentricity at a reference frequency - quantities that can be inferred from the merger events themselves. We investigate the potential constraining power by constructing a constraint atlas spanning a range of system properties and identify the conditions under which the method places tight and reliable bounds on the progenitor triple's outer orbital parameters. By imposing an upper bound on the detector-band eccentricity, we also obtain meaningful constraints for candidate hierarchical mergers proposed in the literature, including GW190514-GW190521. We provide numerical tools for applying the method to user-specified systems and evaluating the reliability of the resulting Peters-based constraints. This framework offers a computationally inexpensive first step toward reconstructing hierarchical-merger progenitors and provides a foundation for extensions incorporating more sophisticated relativistic treatments.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using multipole expansion and re-summation techniques, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.</p>

                <h3>Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Hanxi Wang, Bence Kocsis, Miguel Zumalacárregui</i></p>

            <p>Categories: astro-ph.GA</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.</p>

As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.</p>

First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.</p>

                    <p>Recent interest and realization of ultracold bosons confined in shell-shaped, or bubble, traps have opened up several directions in the study of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) in intrinsically curved geometries. We study an interacting BEC bubble subject to a temporal quench of the interaction strength. We quantify the entanglement of the produced pairs via logarithmic negativity, and show how this measure may be extracted from the power spectrum. These findings establish a bridge between quantum information science and early-universe cosmology in a laboratory setting.</p>

                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.CO</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), a de Sitter (dS) background drives inflation, and the graviton bilinear generates scalar perturbations at second order, with no inflaton or additional fundamental scalar field. We investigate how this scenario can account for the observed scalar spectral tilt. The tensor-mode dependence of the scalar power spectrum gives the consistency relation $n_s-1=2n_T$, since it contains four tensor mode functions. The scalar spectral tilt $n_s\simeq0.9649$ at CMB scales therefore gives $n_T\simeq-0.0175$, independent of the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, hence different from the standard single-field slow-roll prediction $n_T=-r/8$. A full time-dependent calculation of $φ_2$ in exact dS leads to an almost scale-invariant scalar power spectrum, with a small blue infrared residual on the order of $n_s-1\simeq+4\times10^{-4}$. In order to account for the observed red tilt, we introduce a slow drift in the Hubble rate, parametrized by $\varepsilon=-\dot H/H^2$. The tensor tilt is then given by $n_T=-2\varepsilon$, implying $n_s-1\simeq-4\varepsilon$, at leading order. The observed tilt requires $\varepsilon_\ast\simeq0.0088$, far exceeding the drift that can be sustained by the classical graviton backreaction, for which we find $|\varepsilon_{\rm self}|\lesssim10^{-11}$. Therefore, we investigate the quantum break-time of dS as the origin of the background evolution. In this picture, the scalar tilt becomes $n_s-1=-4C_qN_{sp}(H/m_{pl})^2$, where $C_q$ is an order-one depletion coefficient, and the tilt is directly connected to the particle content of dS, $N_{sp}$. The evolution of the drift itself further predicts a positive running of $α_s=+\tfrac12(1-n_s)^2\simeq+6\times10^{-4}$. These results conclude the distinctive observational predictions of the IWI scenario, establishing it as a falsifiable alternative to standard inflaton-driven models.</p>
                </div>

Zimmerman, L. Zimmermann, M. E. Zucker</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We report on a gravitational wave search for compact binary coalescences with secondary mass between 0.2 M and 1 M and primary mass between 0.2 M and 10 M, restricting the component mass ratio to lie between 0.1 and 1. The analysis uses data collected by the LIGO and Virgo detectors between 2024 April 10 15:00:00 and 2025 January 28 17:00:00, the second part of the fourth observing run of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration. Results from two out of three search pipelines show outlier candidates, but not at a sufficient level of significance to provide evidence for detection. We report the combined sensitivity of the current searches over the first and second parts of the observing run to the target sub-solar mass (SSM) black hole (BH) population, as well as to neutron star (NS) binaries with one or more sub-solar component. We place upper limits on the merger rate of SSM BHs, ranging from $50 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to~$5000 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ (90% confidence) for different component mass combinations. We use the merger rate limits to constrain two illustrative dark matter (DM) scenarios that can form SSM compact objects: primordial BHs, and dark BHs forming in a dissipative DM model. Our search limits the fraction of DM in primordial BHs, assuming a monochromatic mass distribution, to be $\leq$ (0.018-0.032) at 1 M, and $\leq$ (0.10-0.18) at 0.35 M for early-forming binaries; or to be less than 1 at masses above (0.62-0.74) M for late-forming binaries. For the dissipative model, we constrain the fraction of DM for a range of minimum dark black hole masses below $1\,M$ to be as low as (1.0-1.1) x $10^{-5}$; we also exclude minimum masses above (0.62-0.74) M, if dark BHs constitute all of the DM. For binary NSs that include sub-solar mass components, assuming a simple, fixed population model we find a merger rate upper limit of $249 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$.</p>

                <h3>Biases in Ringdown Tests of General Relativity from Gravitational-Wave Microlensing</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Sreelakshmi Mundakkal Dasan, Anuj Mishra, Apratim Ganguly</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Gravitational-wave (GW) ringdown signals provide a powerful probe of the strong-field regime of general relativity (GR) through black hole spectroscopy and tests of the Kerr hypothesis. However, unmodeled propagation effects can bias the inference of remnant properties and the interpretation of ringdown features. We investigate the impact of gravitational lensing on ringdown inference and tests of GR using GW150914-like simulated signals spanning the long-wavelength, wave-optics, and geometric-optics regimes. We perform complementary time-domain post-merger and frequency-domain full inspiral--merger--ringdown analyses using unlensed waveform models. We find that lensing in the wave-optics regime can produce substantial biases in the inferred remnant mass and spin and can strongly affect the inferred modal content of the ringdown. In particular, it can spuriously favor the presence of the first overtone, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{221}_{220}\sim40$, even though the injected signal has no support for it. Parameterized ringdown tests can likewise yield strong apparent support for deviations from the Kerr quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{\rm modGR}_{\rm GR}\sim8$. In contrast, the evidence for higher-order modes remains largely unchanged for the simulated signals considered here. The parameterized analysis using the entire signal further shows that microlensing can bias the inferred frequency of the dominant $(2,2,0)$ QNM. These results demonstrate that unmodeled microlensing can produce systematic biases and spurious signatures in ringdown analyses, potentially affecting precision tests of the Kerr hypothesis.</p>

                <h3>Scalar Laplace-Beltrami harmonics and curvature-induced radial mode mixing in Friedmann-like cosmologies</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Eduardo Bittencourt, Peter K. S. Dunsby, Bob Osano, Muzikayise E. Sikhonde</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We develop a harmonic framework for spherically symmetric Friedmann-like geometries with constant scalar curvature but non-zero trace-free Ricci curvature. This preserves Friedmann-type isotropic expansion while introducing a radially varying tidal field and supporting anisotropic stress. We formulate the scalar Laplace-Beltrami operator as a Sturm-Liouville problem and establish its self-adjoint domains and regularity at minimal spheres. Robertson-Walker harmonics are recovered in the maximally symmetric limit. Trace-free curvature terms are expressed as spectral projection kernels. Rotational symmetry preserves angular labels and parity, while the tidal profile couples different radial eigenmodes. A finite-shell calculation displays this off-diagonal structure, verifies consistency between radial representations, and confirms the expected weak-field scaling. A minimally coupled scalar field remains diagonal in the exact basis, indicating operator-dependent mixing rather than mixing solely due to inhomogeneity. We formulate transverse-traceless kernels, whose dynamical application requires a specified model for the supporting anisotropic matter. This converts curvature-induced mode mixing into a spectral problem for perturbations beyond maximally symmetric cosmologies.</p>

            <div>
                <h3>Correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ngo Phuc Duc Loc</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We point out that for black holes (BH) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (GW) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the GW spectrum produced from binary BH mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. In particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from BH mass or population. If BHs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{-1}$ with $M_i$ is the initial BH mass. If BHs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto M_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. Any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new BH physics. The sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm Hz-10^{20}\ \rm Hz$ where both GW spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. As a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular BH model of Hayward featuring a single hair parameter. The observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel BH solution such as Hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. We also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other GW sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.</p>
                </div>

                </div>

                <h3>All Quiet on the Vector Front: Scalar Growth and Perturbative Control in Horndeski--Weyl-squared Gravity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Antonio De Felice, Guillem Domènech, Jan Tränkle</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Higher-order curvature corrections to general relativity arise naturally in many fundamental theories and provide phenomenologically interesting low-energy effective field theories. However, higher-derivative terms can introduce ghost modes, which call the validity of such models into question. Here, we thoroughly investigate the classical linear stability of the most general second-order scalar-tensor theory, namely the Horndeski theory of gravity, augmented by a Weyl-squared term in the action. We consider shift-symmetric de Sitter and power-law FLRW backgrounds and study the evolution of linear perturbations. Vector perturbations are free of gradient and tachyonic instabilities for a positive Weyl-induced mass squared. Tensor perturbations necessarily contain a ghost; their superhorizon branches are bounded, while a frozen-background calculation identifies a separate finite-momentum stability condition. The scalar sector instead contains a growing long-wavelength branch for all expanding backgrounds we consider, which is inherited by at least one of the gauge-invariant Bardeen potentials. We show that this growth enters the Bardeen potentials through an inverse-gradient factor $a^2/k^2$: the dynamical scalar fields remain bounded on the inflationary backgrounds, the direct contribution of the growing shear to the clock-matched tidal field cancels, and the electric part of the Weyl tensor decays. We discuss the implications of our results for perturbative control and for the phenomenological viability of theories including quadratic curvature corrections.</p>

                <h3>Directional effects of the Unruh effect on steering harvesting</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Shu-Min Wu, Rui-Yang Xu, Zhihong Liu</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate directional quantum steering harvesting by two uniformly accelerated non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We show that the Unruh effect does not simply degrade harvested steering, but can reshape its directionality in a strongly parameter-dependent manner. At low detector energy scales, acceleration predominantly suppresses steering, whereas at higher energy scales, moderate acceleration can enhance steering and even activate an initially absent steering direction. Most strikingly, within a finite acceleration window, the Unruh effect enhances steering in one direction while simultaneously suppressing it in the opposite direction, revealing an intrinsically directional influence of relativistic acceleration. Detector non-identicality provides an additional control mechanism: a moderate energy-gap mismatch can enhance or activate one steering direction while suppressing the reverse one, whereas sufficiently large energy-gap mismatch suppresses the harvested steering. Moreover, the maximal steering asymmetry approximately marks the transition from two-way to one-way steering. Our results establish relativistic acceleration and detector non-identicality as means of controlling the strength and directionality of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.</p>

                <h3>Testing Charged Black Holes Embedded in Anisotropic Matter and Surrounded by Plasma through Gravitational Lensing: Bounds from the Sloan Lens ACS Survey</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ritesh Pandey, Shubham Kala, Amare Abebe, Hemwati Nandan, G. G. L. Nashed</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate weak gravitational lensing by a charged black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter, described by the two-component Kiselev metric, and immersed in a homogeneous plasma. We first examine the black hole geometry and horizon structure and then derive the weak-deflection angle from the Hamiltonian description of light propagation in plasma, using an expansion with a fixed turning point that we verify against direct numerical integration. Using the gravitational lens equation, we obtain the Einstein-ring angle, the image positions, the total magnification and the fractional magnifications of the primary and secondary images. We then confront the model with the Einstein radii of two galaxy-scale lenses of the Sloan Lens ACS Survey, J0008$-$0004 and J0029$-$0055. Because the Einstein angle cannot be smaller than the reduced deficit deflection, the observed radii give the mass-independent bounds $K<6.5\times10^{-6}$ and $K<4.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively. The charge correction to the Einstein radius is suppressed by $r_s/R_E\approx 5\times10^{-6}$ and is unobservable, while the plasma parameter at the optical wavelengths of the SLACS imaging is of order $10^{-22}$ and cannot be constrained. Our results show that galaxy-scale strong lensing data place stringent limits on anisotropic matter surrounding the lens, whereas plasma effects can be probed only at low radio frequencies.</p>

            <div>
                <h3>Geodesics in Black-Hole Spacetimes: A Qualitative Classification Using Vieta's Formulae</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Oliver F. Piattella</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>This monograph classifies the geodesics of the Schwarzschild, Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes without solving for their turning points. In all three spacetimes, the radial and polar motions are governed by polynomials whose coefficients depend only on the constants of motion, and the qualitative behavior of a geodesic is fixed by the pattern of their roots. We read this pattern directly off the coefficients, using Vieta's formulae together with the discriminant, Descartes' rule of signs, and the values of the polynomials at the horizons and at infinity. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the reciprocals of the radial roots of every non-radial geodesic add up to $1/(2M)$, which gives the third root of a bound orbit in closed form and the separatrix $p=6+2e$. In Kerr spacetime, the signs of the coefficients show that no radially bound orbit has $\varepsilon^2\geq1$ and that vortical geodesics, timelike or null, have no radial turning point; a positive discriminant is necessary but not sufficient for bound motion, and Descartes' rule applied at the event horizon gives the exact criterion. Spherical orbits and their stability, the equatorial ISCO and light rings, and the photon shell follow from the same relations. In Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, the timelike radial polynomial is a quintic with exactly one negative root, a bound branch requires $\varepsilon^2+ΛL^2/3<1$, and both marginally stable circular orbits lie beyond $6M$. Most of these results are known; the aim is to show that a single, elementary algebraic route leads to all of them. The text is meant for graduate students who have taken a first course in general relativity, and each chapter ends with worked examples.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Quantum noise and torque correlations in a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Yuki Inoue, Mario Onglao, Daiki Tanabe, Masashi Hazumi, Vivek Kumar, Apimook Watcharangkool</i></p>

                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Quantum fluctuations entering through weakly transmitting mirrors can limit a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter for low-frequency gravitational-wave detection, even when its optical layout suppresses radiation-pressure back action. We show that, in the Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS), vacuum fields entering from behind the end and middle test masses can dominate the low-frequency quantum noise despite cancellation of the torques on opposite ends of each bar. For a reference configuration with mirror power transmissions of only $10^{-7}$, these fields contribute $89.7\%$ of the total quantum-noise power spectral density at 0.1 Hz. Omitting them would underestimate the amplitude spectral density by a factor of 3.11. Our input-output model connects the correlations produced by successive optical interactions to the forces on each bar and the measured signal. This connection shows why strong torque cancellation does not, by itself, ensure a corresponding improvement in detector sensitivity. Replacing mirror transmission with absorption at fixed reflectivity leaves the excess quantum noise essentially unchanged for the two operating points studied. The predicted signal response and quantum noise agree with independent FINESSE 3 calculations as recycling detuning and homodyne angle are varied. These results establish rear vacuum fields as a limiting noise source in this torsion-bar speed meter and provide quantitative requirements for its mirror and readout design.</p>

                <h3>Dynamical entropy and thermodynamics of causal diamonds</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Avik Chakraborty, Pratik K. Das, Manavendra Mahato</i></p>

                <div>
                    <p>We study the dynamical entropy of causal diamonds using Wald-Zoupas charges and fluxes on their null boundaries. For a chosen boundary symplectic potential, the boost charge defines an entropy made of an area term plus an expansion correction, which reduces to one quarter of the area at the edge on the diamond. We also examine causal diamonds in maximally symmetric spacetimes and in Einstein-scalar gravity.</p>

                <h3>A catalog of long, eccentric and precessing binary black hole simulations from ICTS-TIFR</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Vaishak Prasad, Prayush Kumar, Michael Boyle, Lawrence E. Kidder, Harald P. Pfeiffer, Mark A. Scheel</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We present a catalogue of 31 binary black hole simulations performed with the Spectral Einstein Code (SpEC) on the Sonic cluster at ICTS-TIFR, Bengaluru between August 2023 and December 2024, targeting the sparsely covered corner of parameter space in which orbital eccentricity and spin-orbit precession are present simultaneously: 17 configurations are both eccentric and precessing, spanning mass ratios $1 \le q \le 11$ and initial eccentricities up to $\hat{e}_0 = 0.40$. The longest, EccPrecDiff002, inspirals for 80 orbits (159 gravitational-wave cycles), to our knowledge the longest simultaneously eccentric and precessing binary black hole evolution to date.   Compile-time optimisation of SpEC and its third-party library stack for the AMD Zen-2 architecture delivered a 90% speedup of the initial-data solver and a 40% speedup of the evolution, roughly half of the latter traceable to a single defect in how pre-2.34 glibc reported cache topology on AMD processors. The campaign consumed $1.18 \times 10^{6}$ CPU-hours.   We document the post-processing pipeline and validate the frame transformation and waveforms. Eccentricity is measured from the waveforms and compared against the initial data. The first law of binary black hole mechanics, a test of approximate helical symmetry, is satisfied to better than 0.54% for every configuration with $e_ω < 0.2$, and we show that even precessing systems can be regarded as possessing approximate helical symmetry in the co-precessing frame. Using the aligned-spin simulations to calibrate the numerical floor, the co-precessing approximation's mirror-symmetry violation lies three to four ordersof magnitude above it, growing from 0.7% to 5.3%with opening angle. EccPrecDiff002 spans the band above 5 Hz without hybridisationfor $M \le 62\,M_\odot$, giving a single-interferometer signal-to-noise ratio of 961 in Cosmic Explorer at 1 Gpc.</p>

                <h3>Hierarchical Parameter Estimation for Intrinsic Parameters of Extreme-mass-ratio Inspirals Using Deep Learning</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ping Shen, Wen-Biao Han, Minghui Du</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) stand as prime targets for future space-borne gravitational wave (GW) detectors, yet their precise parameter estimation is severely hindered by waveform complexity and high-dimensional parameter spaces. In this work, we propose a deep learning framework capable of recovering the seven intrinsic EMRI parameters without relying on detailed priors for extrinsic parameters. Our approach first employs a U-Net to extract robust signal features from noisy time-frequency data. These features are then fed into a multi-channel convolutional neural network (CNN) equipped with a dual attention mechanism, which decouples the time and frequency dimensions to jointly model long-range temporal evolution and persistent spectral structures, thereby enhancing sensitivity to EMRI time-frequency ridges in noisy data. Remarkably, this method reduces the search ranges for the parameters $\{\log M, a, μ, e_0, p_0 \}$ and $\{t_p, {x_I}_0 \}$ by factors of $\sim 10^{2}$ and $\sim 10^{1}$, respectively, effectively shrinking the total volume of the seven-dimensional parameter space by $\sim 10^{8}$. Such a dramatic reduction enables a rapid pre-screening of the intrinsic parameter space, substantially saving computational cost for subsequent full parameter estimation. Although our framework is developed with Taiji mission specifications in mind, the methodology is applicable to data from other space-borne GW detectors.</p>

                <h3>General Relativity in Three Lines</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Pawel Nurowski</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: math-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We show that complex general relativity can be formulated directly in terms of three affine lines assigned to each spacetime point. The lines are represented by Plücker bivectors, and Urbantke's construction applied to the associated two-forms reconstructs the conformal spacetime metric. Starting from the chiral Plebański action, the simplicity constraints turn the three two-forms into a null internal basis of simple bivectors and thereby into three projective lines. A $3+1$ decomposition then yields a first-order canonical theory whose configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines and whose conjugate variable is a line momentum. The resulting constraint system consists of three internal Gauss constraints, three vector constraints, and one Hamiltonian constraint.   A notable feature of the line formulation is that the equation obtained by varying the line momentum is pointwise algebraic after the spatial integrations by parts. Consequently the momentum can be eliminated explicitly wherever the corresponding Legendre map is invertible, giving a second-order action whose only dynamical configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines. The line curvature separates naturally into a cosmological trace and the Weyl matrix of the selected chiral sector. The Legendre map becomes singular on a distinguished null-evolution locus where the spacetime metric remains nondegenerate. There its rank drops from nine to six, giving three algebraic compatibility conditions. We construct a finite invariant partial Legendre transform and a smooth constrained second-order continuation through this locus. This analysis provides a regular framework for regimes in which the evolution direction becomes null and may be useful in the study of near-horizon geometries and related gravitational phenomena.</p>

                <h3>Tidal deformability of white dwarfs in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Santanu Pradhan, Tapobrata Sarkar</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We compute the static quadrupole Love number $k_2$ and the dimensionless tidal deformability $Λ$ of cold white dwarfs in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld (EiBI) gravity. Matter couples to the physical metric while perturbation equations are solved in an auxiliary metric, so the physical tidal field near the surface depends on derivatives of the equation of state. This dependence is regular for a surface polytropic index $1<Γ_{\rm env}<3/2$, but not for the $Γ= 5/3$ Chandrasekhar equation of state. The mechanism, an algebraic map between the metric that carries perturbations and the metric that matter feels, is common to Palatini-type theories, so the same type of surface condition should apply to tidal calculations in this wider class. We use thermodynamically consistent envelopes that exactly reach zero enthalpy. At five masses from \(0.6\) to \(1.3\,\Msun\) and five sampled Born-Infeld couplings \(κ\), with $|κ|\le5\times10^6\,\mathrm{m^2}$, the EiBI-GR differences are approximately linear in $κ$. The largest absolute fractional shifts are \(3.89\times 10^{-5}\) in the stellar radius $R$, \(4.09\times 10^{-5}\) in $k_2$, and \(2.36\times 10^{-4}\) in $Λ$. Across nine envelope models, half the spread of each quantity relative to the baseline envelope is at most \(0.0186\) in $R$ and \(0.0857\) in \(k_2\), but only \(3.02\times 10^{-5}\) in \(Λ\) as the changes in \(k_2\) and \(R^5\) largely cancel. A high-precision calculation shows that the envelope dependence of the EiBI-GR difference in \(Λ\) is small. Half the spread of this difference ranges from \(1.067\times 10^{-12}\) to \(6.208\times 10^{-11}\) over the 20 nonzero mass-coupling points.</p>

                <h3>A quantum probabilistic approach to the emergence of an inflationary Starobinsky Universe</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Eftychios Kaimakkamis</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-14</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We propose that the necessary conditions for the existence of inflation could be explained by a quantum probabilistic approach. We interpret physical states $ψ$ obtained via the path integral formulation as probability density amplitudes for the Universe to be measured at a particular geometric configuration. First, we examine the problem of ordering ambiguities in the Wheeler-DeWitt (WDW) equation. We develop a formalism to handle ambiguities in the canonical quantization of a $1d$ minisuperspace by defining ambiguity functions within the WDW equation. We define a Hilbert space inner product for calculating physical observables, and using an argument from the hermiticity of the Hamiltonian, we obtain an expression for its measure $μ$ in addition to constraints on the ambiguity functions. By defining a new quantum state $Ψ=\sqrtμ ψ$ and using the path integral formalism, we are able to resolve ambiguities and prove the theory is universal. We then generalize for any $M$-dimensional minisuperspace system, for which we can prove universality in the semi-classical approximation for a large class of models. We also show that this universality extends to all orders of quantum theory if the target space manifold of the theory is flat. We calculate probability amplitudes for various cosmological scenarios involving Starobinsky inflation. We summarize the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary proposal for GR and we comment on the distinct possibilities of defining a contour of integration: the sign choice of Hartle-Hawking vs that of Linde-Vilenkin. We make an analogous calculation for $R^{2}$ gravity and find that for the Linde- Vilenkin choice it is statistically more likely for the Universe to emerge in its inflationary stage. Finally, we calculate transition amplitudes when the kinetic energy of the inflaton field $φ$ takes non-zero values.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>In this article we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory. String theory, according to this view, originates in foundations of quantum theory and Nambu's dynamics, which features in the non-perturbative definition of string theory in terms of a T-duality covariant and non-commutative formulation, called the metastring. Nambu's dynamics and the associated cubic and hypercubic objects also appear as the natural language for exploring the new observables and phenomena implied by a dynamical Born rule, including triple and higher order quantum interference, that can be investigated in experiments involving massive quantum probes, and that are also needed for direct empirical tests of the Born rule, a cornerstone of quantum theory.</p>

                <h3>Detectability of Gravitational Waves from Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals on Periodic Orbits around Bardeen Black Holes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Li Huang, Xing He</i></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate gravitational wave (GW) signatures from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a Bardeen black hole, modeling the small object as a test particle, and provide a framework for probing strong-field spacetime geometry. We first present the equations of motion for test particles around a Bardeen black hole and characterize circular orbits in the parameter space of energy and angular momentum. Using Levin's classification, we adopt the extended classification scheme to classify periodic orbits around a Bardeen black hole. We then compute GW waveforms in both the time and frequency domains, as well as the corresponding characteristic strains, for these periodic orbits and compare them with the sensitivity curves of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), the evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (eLISA), the TianQin mission, the Big Bang Observer (BBO), and the Decihertz Interferometer Gravitational wave Observatory (DECIGO). We find that detectability is controlled primarily by the luminosity distance. At a luminosity distance of 200 Mpc, the signals can exceed the sensitivity curves of BBO and DECIGO and are comparable to the LISA sensitivity curve, whereas at 2 Gpc, they remain below the sensitivity curves of all detectors considered. These results suggest that EMRIs on periodic orbits around Bardeen black holes offer a promising avenue to probe strong-field gravity and the properties of Bardeen black holes.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Hydrodynamic fluctuations in the primordial plasma generate a gravitational-wave (GW) background that grows like $f^3_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ in terms of the current frequency. However, within the ($10^{-4}_{ } ... 10^4_{ })\,$Hz band of upcoming interferometers, the modes likely re-entered the Hubble horizon when the hydrodynamic noise was no longer at its maximal value. Following previous estimates, we find that a pre-exit-generated hydrodynamic tail becomes almost flat below $(10^5_{ } ... 10^7_{ })\;$Hz. Its small-$f^{ }_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ intercept remains finite, and can then moderately influence observational constraints through the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$).</p>

                <h3>Linear stability matrix and Lyapunov exponents for stationary spacetime</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Xu Ye, Shao-Wen Wei</i></p>

            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Lyapunov exponents characterize the average rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge and therefore provide a useful criterion for dynamical stability. In this work, we develop a general framework for analyzing Lyapunov exponents in stationary spacetimes and extend previous studies beyond circular orbits. For a generic stationary spacetime described by $g_{μν}(r,θ)$, we show that the phase space relevant to linear perturbations is spanned by $(r,p_r,θ,p_θ)$ and the corresponding linear stability matrix has rank four. When the spacetime admits a rank-2 Killing tensor, the linear stability matrix can be reduced to a block-diagonal form, allowing the Lyapunov exponents to be obtained analytically. By imposing the appropriate constraint conditions, the formalism further yields the linear stability matrices and Lyapunov exponents for circular and spherical orbits. The validity of the method is illustrated by several representative examples, including the (inverted) harmonic oscillator, planar Kepler motion, and particle motion in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes. These results provide a unified framework for investigating the stability properties of particle orbits in both classical and relativistic dynamical systems.</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Gravity from entropy (GfE) identifies its Lagrangian with the geometric quantum relative entropy (GQRE) between the spacetime metric and a metric induced by matter and curvature, treating the metric itself as a quantum operator. We extend this construction to the Tsallis, Rényi, and Sharma-Mittal families, which we call gravity from generalized entropy (GfGE), and determine their common Einstein limit, weak-field spectra, auxiliary-field formulation, and horizon entropy. The entropy choice controls the leading higher-curvature terms and additional modes. We confirm that the linearized GfE spectrum contains a healthy scalar and a Planck-scale tachyonic spin-2 ghost. We identify the conditions that remove this ghost: curvature must enter through its scalar trace, or the entropy generator must be flat to quadratic order at the identity. The latter gives exact general relativity for Tsallis at $q=0$ and ghost-free $f(R,L_m)$ theories for Rényi and Sharma-Mittal. On shell, the auxiliary G-field is proportional to the tensor in Wald's entropy formula. For analytic entropy functions, horizons with a single curvature scale have an area term followed by constant and inverse-area corrections. We also extend the volume-constraint cosmological constant to the full family; its leading entropy dependence is set by the scalar mass. A finite set of entropy-function derivatives controls the leading weak-curvature departures from general relativity.</p>

                <h3>The WDM time-frequency transform in gravitational-wave data analysis II: Evolutionary spectrum and noise covariance</h3>
                <div>

                <div>
                    <p>Noise cannot be treated as stationary over the timescales required for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors, minutes for ground-based and months for space-based detectors. Nonstationarity leads to a non-diagonal frequency-domain noise covariance matrix, thus motivating a shift to the time-frequency domain. We introduce \emph{evolutionary power spectra} for describing nonstationary noise in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency basis. Under the framework of oscillatory processes, we show that, to leading order in the ratio of the Meyer filter and the nonstationarity timescales, the evolutionary spectrum is a power-frequency distribution that can be estimated from a single noise realization. We derive the corresponding noise covariance matrix and show that it is band tri-diagonal, like its stationary counterpart. The exact covariance to all orders is positive semi-definite by construction and dense depending on the noise. We further derive the optimal tiling of the time-frequency plane that minimizes the error of a diagonal covariance approximation and show that coarse-graining the plane suppresses correlations quadratically. Using simulated data with a LISA Galactic foreground and a drifting powerlaw spectrum, we show that the stationarity approximation leads to signal-to-noise ratio loss and severely biases inference. For realistic LISA data, approximating the covariance as diagonal in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer domain is accurate for the narrow-band analysis of a single resolved Galactic binary, but insufficient for a broad-band analysis. Finally, we provide mitigation strategies for the wraparound correlations induced across the data time edges whenever the spectrum differs between the start and the end of the data.</p>

                <h3>The Forgetful Black Hole: Memory Burden and Hysteresis in Hawking Evaporation</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Yen Chin Ong</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The memory-burden scenario of black hole evaporation proposes that Hawking emission may become increasingly suppressed as maintaining stored quantum information becomes dynamically costly. In this work, we revisit this scenario and investigate the conditions under which information retention can produce a genuine dynamical burden. We derive general scaling conditions for incremental memory accumulation at a fixed fractional mass loss and establish a conditional no-go result: entropy-suppressed, zero-mean deposits with subextensive integrated correlations cannot produce an order-one luminosity modification through unamplified accumulation and bounded feedback. We identify three essential requirements for dynamical memory: a record of the past must be written, retained, and coupled back to subsequent evaporation. We illustrate these requirements with concrete toy models that exhibit either a prolonged but finite black hole lifetime or an asymptotically approached finite-mass state (an effective remnant). We further distinguish kinetic-memory, thermodynamic-memory, and spectral-memory sub-categories of possible memory-burden mechanisms. In particular, we demonstrate that an independently evolving memory variable can generate evaporation-accretion hysteresis, such that a black hole returning to the same mass may possess a different retained memory and consequently a different luminosity. This history dependence may have implications for primordial black hole phenomenology. Finally, we briefly discuss the possibility of "merger rejuvenation", in which black hole mergers reorganize or reset the effective memory state.</p>
                </div>

                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18997v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.18997v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>Black Hole Fine Structure</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Adrian Ka-Wai Chung, Richard Dyer, Tomasz Kinowski, Christopher J. Moore</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>In General Relativity, axial and polar black-hole perturbations share identical quasinormal-mode spectra, a property known as isospectrality. New physics can break this degeneracy, producing a spectral splitting analogous to atomic fine structure. We perform a theory-agnostic search for such splitting in gravitational-wave observations. We find no evidence for isospectrality breaking and place a combined $90\%$ upper limit of $<28.5\%$ on the relative frequency splitting. We map these constraints onto several modified-gravity theories, constraining the coupling-lengths to be $\lesssim 28\,\mathrm{km}$.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>Scalar-Assisted Growth of Supermassive Black Holes: Boson-Mass Windows and Observational Constraints</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Jorge Castelo Mourelle, Darío Núñez Zúñiga, Saeed Fakhry, Nicolas Sanchis-Gual</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.CO</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study a phenomenological cosmological model of black-hole growth in which a finite baryonic reservoir and a bosonic scalar cloud feed the black hole simultaneously. The baryonic component accretes through an Eddington-like channel, while the scalar cloud transfers mass through an effective quasibound-state decay rate. Evolving the system directly in redshift within a flat $Λ$CDM background, we scan over $μ$, $M_0$, $M_{c,0}$, and $M_{b,0}$ to assess whether scalar-assisted accretion can accelerate the formation of $10^9M_\odot$ supermassive black holes. We find that the scalar contribution is highly selective in parameter space. For the mass scales explored here, scalar transfer is most efficient for $μ\sim10^{-19}-10^{-16} \mathrm{eV}$, producing rapid cloud depletion and significantly earlier black-hole growth, while outside this interval the evolution remains mainly baryonic. More generally, this efficient window reflects a preferred range of the dimensionless coupling $α=μM_{\rm BH}$ and therefore shifts approximately as $μ\propto M_{\rm BH}^{-1}$. Comparison with observed quasar masses and luminosities instead favors lower boson masses, broadly around $μ\sim10^{-21}-10^{-20}\mathrm{eV}$. These results are not necessarily in tension, since the boson mass that maximizes early growth depends on the characteristic black-hole mass and evolutionary stage. This separation between dynamical efficiency and observational compatibility leaves open complementary roles for different bosonic mass scales in supermassive black hole growth and dark-matter phenomenology.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>Strong-Field Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Ray-Traced Arrival-Time Surfaces</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Luka Vujeva, João S. Santos, Brian C. Seymour</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The diffraction integral formalism has been greatly successful in describing gravitational wave lensing effects in scenarios where the wavelength of the signal is comparable to the characteristic length scale of the lens, known as the wave optics regime. However, the assumptions required to construct its integrand break down as the source approaches the strong gravity region of a black hole lens. In particular, we are interested in the lensed signal from a binary (the source) near a massive black hole (the lens). We present a new formalism for obtaining low frequency corrections to sources being lensed in the strong field regime of gravity by leveraging the fact that null geodesics obey the Hamilton--Jacobi equations. In doing so, we are able to construct a time delay surface without relying on the thin lens approximation, and solve the diffraction integral for the resulting surface directly. For a stationary source at $10M$, deep in the strong field regime, when comparing the results with a relativistic wave scattering model, we find $6.5\%$ and $0.3\%$ agreement in the peak amplification and first diffractive fringe, respectively. Furthermore, we find a $< 1\%$ agreement with the amplitude of the point mass lens with a source at $10^4 M$ in the weak field, but noticeable dephasing between the peaks of the amplification function at higher frequencies. This work allows for clean interpolation between otherwise separate regimes, valid for sources from $\sim 6M \to \infty$. It provides a transparent, physically motivated framework for computing beyond-geometric optics lensing effects in the strong field regime.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>Thin shells in Lovelock and Quasi-topological gravities</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Pablo Bueno, Pablo A. Cano, Robie A. Hennigar, Ángel J. Murcia, Aitor Vicente-Cano</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We derive the junction conditions for spherically symmetric thin shells in Lovelock and Quasi-topological gravities along two independent routes: from the distributional form of the field equations, and from the boundary term that makes the variational problem well-posed in the non-null case. The former method is ambiguous as it stands, since the equations contain products of Heaviside step functions with a Dirac delta. We show that the singular parts of the field equations are exact differentials in the jumping variables, so that the Vol'pert chain rule for functions of bounded variation fixes these singular combinations uniquely and no products of two deltas survive for a single shell, finding that both routes then agree. The same rule yields the null junction conditions, for which no boundary term is available in Quasi-topological gravities, together with the mass conservation law of the shell. These results clarify recent questions concerning the existence of thin shells in these theories. In particular, we show that previous claims that the junction conditions force the shell mass to vary with radius are incorrect and arise from treating a trapezoidal approximation to the relevant distributional products as exact. Our results also provide a basis for the recent analyses of mass inflation in these theories.</p>

                <h3>Spinformation: do gravitational-wave events carry information beyond effective spins?</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Cailin Plunkett, Jack Heinzel, Noah E. Wolfe, Davide Gerosa, Salvatore Vitale</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>While the spin vectors of binary black holes offer insight into the astrophysical formation channels of these systems, individual spins are less precisely measured through gravitational-wave observations than the effective inspiral spin $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and the effective precession spin $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Reducing to effective parameters discards information in the data, but how much information is lost has yet to be demonstrated. Here we show how to quantify whether individual mergers carry information about component spins beyond the constraints implied by effective parameters (a.k.a. spinformation) and apply the technique to GWTC-5. Thresholding on information loss $\gtrsim 0.25$ bits, over $80\%$ of gravitational-wave events in GWTC-5 have component spin posteriors described by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ alone. Only $\sim3\%$ of gravitational-wave events have substantial spin information not explained by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. The catalog's component spin information is effectively two-dimensional in $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Using simulated signals, we find the noise realization can create or destroy over a bit of beyond-$χ_\mathrm{eff}$ information: the structure in real data may therefore be driven by noise. At current sensitivity, component spins provide interpretive\textemdash rather than informational\textemdash advantage over effective parameters.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Strong Field Gravitational Lensing in Full Wave Optics</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>João Sieiro dos Santos, Luka Vujeva</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Compact binaries evolving in the vicinity of massive black holes may be commonplace in the Universe, and their gravitational waves carry signatures of their environment. We study the strong lensing of these signals by the massive companion, a configuration that violates the standard assumptions of the lensing literature: geometric optics and thin lenses. Using a perturbative framework, we compute the full wave optics amplification factors for face-on and edge-on binaries, including spinning lenses. In the edge-on configuration, peak amplification does not occur at perfect source--lens--observer alignment, even for a non-spinning lens. This is a consequence of the anisotropic, coherent quadrupolar emission of the stellar-mass binary breaking the axisymmetry of the system. Restricting to the equatorial plane near the optical axis, we then find that the frequency dependence of the amplification factor is universal across every configuration studied, persisting deep into the wave optics regime. Comparing against a strong-field ray tracing calculation, we find agreement at the $\sim10\%$ level for a face-on binary lensed by a Schwarzschild black hole. In the less symmetric edge-on case only the angular peak shift and fringe spacing is reproduced to this accuracy. For a Kerr lens, the face-on amplification factor is described by its Schwarzschild counterpart to the same $\sim 10 \%$ accuracy once the effect of frame dragging is corrected for. A point mass lens, by contrast, fails to reproduce the features of the system, which may have strong implications for forecasts that adopt it for lensing by massive black holes in the strong field.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Identity Crisis: Untangling Mass-Ordering Artifacts from Compact-Object Pairing in Gravitational-Wave Populations</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Soumendra Kishore Roy, Asad Hussain, L. A. C. van Son, Maya Fishbach, Carl L. Rodriguez, Will M. Farr</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.HE</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Mass distributions of binary black hole mergers inferred from gravitational-wave observations offer clues to how binaries form. These distributions conventionally label the heavier component as the primary, with mass $m_1$, and the lighter as the secondary, with mass $m_2$, such that $m_1 \geq m_2$. This ordering folds the physically labeled mass distribution along the equal-mass line, potentially reshaping the underlying population structure. In this Letter, we determine which population features can arise from mass ordering and which require genuine astrophysical structure. We show that ordering alone can produce (1) an $m_2$ distribution that declines more rapidly than the $m_1$ distribution, without intrinsic differences between the physically labeled components, and (2) an apparent concentration along equal masses, without correlations that preferentially pair black holes of equal mass. Moreover, different physically labeled populations can produce the same ordered mass distribution. Crucially, however, a preferred companion mass that remains constant as $m_1$ increases requires a characteristic mass scale already present in the physically labeled population. Applied to binary black hole mergers in the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, our model recovers such a scale near $m_2 \simeq 50\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. Around this scale, the merger-rate density declines much more rapidly toward higher $m_2$ than toward lower $m_2$, ruling out an equal or weaker high-$m_2$ decline at 99.45% credibility. This structure therefore requires a characteristic mass scale in at least one physically labeled component, but masses alone cannot determine which component carries it. Any formation model reproducing the observed high-mass binary black hole merger population must contain such a scale.</p>
                </div>

                </div>

            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>EMRIs in Kerr Spacetime: The Role of Inclination Diffusion</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Yael Alush, Nicholas C. Stone, Scott A. Hughes</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.GA</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are expected to be a major source of gravitational waves (GWs) for the future {\it Laser Interferometer Space Antenna} ({\it LISA}). An EMRI occurs when a compact object, driven by the emission of gravitational radiation, slowly inspirals into a massive black hole (MBH). The classical formation channel involves repeated two-body interactions within dense nuclear star clusters. However, both EMRI event rates and the expected distribution of their orbital parameters remain highly uncertain. A major source of this uncertainty is the poorly constrained ratio between gradually inspiraling EMRIs and direct plunges, which do not produce detectable GWs. While most studies of astrophysical EMRI production focus on the Schwarzschild limit, previous work examining the Kerr metric found that the spin of the central MBH can significantly affect the EMRI-to-plunge ratio. This enhancement depends sensitively on orbital inclination, yet earlier studies held inclination fixed. In this work, we develop the mathematical framework describing inclination evolution driven by two-body encounters evolving along Kerr geodesics. By implementing 3D diffusion into Monte Carlo simulations, we show that initially prograde orbits may evolve into retrograde states, thereby converting potential EMRIs into plunges or vice versa. We estimate the EMRI-to-plunge ratio and find that substantial MBH spin enhances the EMRI rate by a factor of $\sim 2.5$. Additionally, even for a non-spinning MBH, modeling the orbits as relativistic geodesics rather than Newtonian trajectories increases the number of EMRIs by a similar factor of $\sim 2.5$. The distribution of Kerr EMRI inclinations has a substantial prograde bias that may aid in identifying the subset of loss cone EMRIs within large future EMRI samples.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Nonlinear Perturbations of Relativistic Stars</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>K. J. Kwon, Abhishek Hegade K. R., Tejaswi Venumadhav, Hang Yu, Nicolás Yunes</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We extend the general relativistic Lagrangian perturbation formalism of Friedman and Schutz [Astrophys. J. 200, 204 (1975)] beyond linear order, retaining full time dependence of the perturbations. We provide general formulae to relate the Lagrangian and Eulerian perturbations to any general perturbative order. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to tidally perturbed relativistic stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge and reduce the second-order field and conservation equations to master equations with a nonlinear source. Projecting the source onto the star's eigenmodes, we obtain a nonlinear equation of motion for the mode amplitudes and the coupling coefficients, which describe the interactions among the eigenmodes and with the external tidal field. Approximating the tidal field and the coupling coefficients, we compute the static quadratic Love number from the quadrupolar fundamental mode alone and find that it reproduces the direct metric-matching value to a reasonable accuracy of $4\%$, up to a further correction arising from the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of the second-order tidal field.</p>

                <h3>Separation of gravitational perturbations of singly spinning Myers-Perry black holes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Jorge E. Santos</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-10-13</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Gravitational perturbations of rotating black holes in higher dimensions generally obey coupled partial differential equations. We show that scalar gravitational perturbations invariant under rotations of the transverse sphere of a singly spinning Myers-Perry black hole separate, despite the obstruction to a decoupled Teukolsky equation. Two commuting, second-order angular operators organise the three gauge-invariant curvature components into joint eigenfunctions. The physical radial problem is a $2\times2$ first-order system, equivalent to a single second-order equation. This gives a separation of the sector containing both the bar-mode and axisymmetric ultraspinning instabilities. Using only ordinary differential equations, we compute the bar-mode quasinormal spectrum in $d=5,6,7$ and find instability onsets at $a/r_+=0.90498$ and $0.83228$ in $d=6,7$. We also compute the growing axisymmetric modes and their onset rotations in $d=6,\ldots,9$. The construction shows how separability can survive the coupling between gravitational polarisations.</p>
